reason: Nothing was lost: V1 GroupPermissions.canView(group) already checks canView()||canManage() first, and V2 canView(group) checks the MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles and falls back to the all-groups resource, so dropping canViewGlobal changes nothing. The old code did not pass view rights from a parent group down to its subgroups either, so the 'hierarchy' change it describes is not a regression.

The listener is registered only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) is on, and the PR only moved that check, which already existed inside onEvent. Keycloak treats ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and _V2 as v1/v2 of the same versioned feature and does not allow both to be enabled, so the listener never reaches GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled in the 'both on' case.

True: GroupPermissions lines 50-52 duplicate the MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP/MANAGE_MEMBERS/VIEW_MEMBERS strings that the PR adds to AdminPermissionsSchema. But it is a maintainability nit and the finding itself says it is not a functional bug.

The PR changes error-invalid-multivalued-size in the keycloak.v3 account file (and the same key in the admin-ui v2 file) from '{{0}}...{{2}} value(s)' to Java MessageFormat '{0}...{2} {2,choice,...}'. Every other parameterised error in these i18next bundles uses {{0}}, so i18next will not fill in the values and users will see the raw placeholders and choice syntax.

True that santizeAnchors removes <a> tags before the OWASP policy runs, so hrefs are never scheme-checked. But a translated anchor is only accepted if it is byte-identical to the anchor in the trusted English source, so no realistic unsafe href gets through; this is a hardening suggestion.

missing_backup_codes tells users to 'generate them in your settings', but the PR only creates codes in setup.ts during 2FA enable and has no regenerate UI or endpoint. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration (backupCodes null) get an instruction they cannot follow, and on the login 'Lost access' path they cannot reach settings at all.

Same issue as fp15: there is no regenerate control anywhere in the PR. Codes are made only in setup.ts and set to null in disable.ts, so the 'generate them in your settings' message (used in login.tsx and DisableTwoFactorModal) points at a feature that does not exist.

True: saveChanges calls embedding.update({}), Admin::EmbeddingController#update only re-renders, and neither embedding.hbs nor the component template uses saveChanges. It is dead code with no runtime failure.

A missing empty-state message is a UX nit. The claimed serializer breakage is wrong: the PR's store.js _hydrateEmbedded change turns the embeddable_host_ids from `embed: :ids` into an embeddable_hosts array of hydrated records.

embed_url comes from an anonymous request param (the referer check can be spoofed). TopicRetriever#invalid_host? checks only URI(url).host before TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url), and open-uri follows redirects without re-checking, so an open redirect on the embeddable host lets the server fetch internal URLs and import their content as a public post. This is a different call site from the golden's PollFeed/feed_polling_url SSRF.

The points are accurate (URI host case not normalised, same-parent-domain hosts treated as siblings, a trailing '/' kept), but website_name only decides whether the path is shown in a display label. The a.example.com/b.example.com case is the branch's intended behaviour.

FallbackLocaleList#[] makes the fallback chain depend on SiteSetting.default_locale. The I18n.translate LRU cache key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{backend.object_id}", so fallback results cached under the old default locale (or another site's, in multisite) are served until they are evicted. The impact is limited to keys missing from the user's locale.

getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is typed (credentialIds: number[]), so nullable credentialIds would not type-check. connectedCalendars entries carry the credential's numeric id. Prisma `in: []` simply returns no rows, and a query covering non-Google credentials is harmless, so no failure follows.

scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh sets ENV_FILE="../.env" relative to the current directory. Running it from the repo root touches or creates a .env outside the repo (line 64), and the app never gets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Real, but it only affects a dev helper script.

dev:cron did change to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` and tsx is not in apps/web/package.json. Whether it is hoisted from the monorepo root is not visible, and at worst npx fetches tsx for a dev-only cron tester script.

It is true that NewResourceServer returns on an s.Init error without calling cancel. But ctx is just WithCancel(Background): the backend Init only pings the DB and the search watcher uses its own context.Background(), so nothing is bound to it, and a failed constructor aborts startup anyway.

BuildIndex's `_, span :=` line is unchanged context. The builder callback is a closure that captures ctx from searchSupport.build (which now does `ctx, span := ...`) and takes no ctx argument, so the ListIterator work is already under the Build span. Capturing ctx in BuildIndex would change nothing, and the trace is not disconnected.

It is true that the Mode3 tests never wait for or assert the goroutine's Legacy.* calls. However, legacy and storage share one mock.Mock, so AssertCalled could not tell them apart anyway. This is a test-coverage gap, not a defect in the changed production code.

Same test-coverage gap as fp17: there is no sync or assertion on the async legacy calls. Its sub-claim that the error case's Legacy Create expectation is unused is wrong: ls and us share mock m, so storage.Create(failingObj) consumes that expectation and produces the error.

This is speculative. The new clause only reads getConfig() when getOrganizationId() != null. The existing HIDE_ON_LOGIN/LINK_ONLY filters in the same predicate already go through config-backed model getters, and IdentityProviderModel's config defaults to a non-null map. No concrete path produces a null config.

update() passes getById()'s org-aware wrapper to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate. That wrapper's isEnabled() is false when the org is disabled, so an update that sets hideOnLogin/linkOnly or clears broker-public fails both predicate checks and skips invalidation. Infinispan getForLogin then serves the stale cached id list without re-filtering, and the bean only re-checks isEnabled(), so after the org is re-enabled the hidden or link-only IdP appears on the login page.

Both target the stats write (match_count/last_match_at + record.save) inside BlockedEmail.should_block?, which is called from the email validator. That matches the golden 'BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects...'. The finding's save-vs-save! contrast is also inaccurate: in Rails both roll back on validation failure.

The finding itself confirms that every ANY(${array}) use is guarded (teamIds always contains orgId, and the user-id arrays are checked with length > 0). Postgres `= ANY('{}')` is also valid SQL that evaluates to false, not a syntax error. This is speculation about future changes.

get_failure_reason and get_monitor_environment_context were moved to incident_occurrence.py, not deleted, and SimpleCheckIn moved to types.py. The finding names no importer or test that actually breaks: produce_occurrence_to_kafka was a function-local import, so it was never patchable on the mark_failed module.

readLength() rejects long-form lengths >= limit (the decoder's input size), so the allocation in read(length) can never exceed the input size. Short-form lengths are at most 127, and running out of input throws IOException in read(). Comparing against the whole input rather than the remaining bytes is a hardening nit with no realistic failure, and the code mirrors BouncyCastle's ASN1InputStream.

True that the test signs with one default KeyPairGenerator("EC") key (P-256) for ES256/384/512 and only round-trips through the provider's own decoder and encoder. But concatenatedRSToASN1DER, integerToBytes and ASN1Encoder.writeLength (long form for lengths over 127) are correct for 48- and 66-byte R/S values, so the weaker test hides no bug. This is a test-coverage suggestion.

Same observation as fp16: ECDSAAlgorithmTest reuses one P-256 key and never calls Signature.verify. The padding and truncation logic in integerToBytes and the DER long-form length encoding check out on inspection, so no concrete defect goes undetected. It is only a test-quality improvement.

Line 64 guards only on FileHelper.is_image?(filename). The snapshot treats SVG as an image: create_thumbnails is enqueued for is_image? files, and OptimizedImage.create_for special-cases .svg to copy it instead of running convert. So an SVG larger than max_image_size_kb (previously rejected) is now run through convert -resize 80% in place, which rasterizes or mangles the vector. The ignored downsize return value is a smaller point, since an oversized file would still fail upload validation.

Same root issue as the golden 'Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']...'. The PR replaces the setting-based limit with a hardcoded 10MB, and this finding points at the server-side counterpart: FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) on line 55, which ignores the per-type settings.

Accurate that unsubscribe steps watching/tracking down to regular (line 107: if level > regular then regular, else muted), so reply and mention notifications continue. This is a deliberate step-down design, and the page shows the notifications button to change the level further. It is a wording/product-semantics nit, not a defect.

The code does not toggle. With muted=0 and regular=1, a muted topic fails 'level > regular' and is set to muted again, and regular goes to muted. Repeated visits only lower the level (watching to regular to muted) and never resume notifications. The action also requires a logged-in user, so link prefetchers cannot trigger it.

The finding assumes the frontend applyTemplateVariables replaces $__range. The PR's own guard comment (querySplitting.ts lines 285-286) says $__range 'is interpolated on the backend', and Loki's applyTemplateVariables strips __range/__range_s/__range_ms from scopedVars for that reason. The token therefore survives and isQueryWithRangeVariable still fires. The shard path also already passed interpolated queries into runSplitQuery before this PR.

True that runShardSplitQuery now filters on the raw expr before interpolating (lines 49-52), so a query whose expr is a single variable resolving to '' is not dropped there. But the claimed outcome, being sent for execution, does not follow: runSplitQuery re-filters on the already-interpolated expr (line 298) and drops it. In runSplitQuery the filter already ran before interpolation before this PR. Narrow edge case.

APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED does evaluate to the encryption-key string, not a boolean. Every usage (app-credential.ts:19, parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15, refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5) is a truthiness check and the value is never logged or serialized, so no leak or misbehaviour exists today. Wrapping it in !!() is a style/defensive nit.

The described failure contradicts the code. UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate() sets or removes the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH note on every run (lines 102/104). badPasswordHandler only calls context.clearUser() when clearUser = !isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth, i.e. when the note is not 'true', so the 'user cleared but note still true' state cannot occur. The rest is speculation about stale notes after a flow restart.

Confirmed: the alias-level combo-box sits outside {{#if id}} in group.hbs, and Group.create() posts asJSON() including alias_level, but Admin::GroupsController#create (lines 22-32) sets only name and visible. A level chosen at creation is silently lost. The old create also ignored it, but this PR rewrote create and kept the omission.

Speculative: .extra-info-wrapper is the flex child of the header's .contents (which now gets flexbox + align-items:center), so order(2) does apply, and the finding names no concrete other context where removing the bullet margin-top breaks layout.

.small-action now gets @include flexbox() while `button { float: right; }` is unchanged and .small-action-desc has no flex-grow. Floats on flex items are ignored, and a non-growing desc shrinks to its content, so the delete/edit button no longer sits at the right edge. This is a cosmetic regression.

Same root cause as the golden 'Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues... removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel'. .panel loses float:right and keeps only margin-left:auto, with no fallback wherever flex auto-margins don't apply. The finding cites old browsers rather than the noscript header.

The PR raises the deadline, it does not add one: check_auth_identities previously used the taskworker default processing deadline (10s), and this change sets it to 60s, the same pattern the PR applies in deliver_webhooks.py. The risk of a slow batch being killed already existed and is reduced, so the change is not a regression.

Self-refuting: the finding itself concludes 'This is correct behavior' for both the loading and the not-found paths, and the code (enabled requires project?.slug, plus the `replayRecord?.project_id && !project` guard) matches that.

The `if (updateStrategy == null) return kc;` path is unchanged context: with no update spec the CR behaves exactly as before. The PR has no operator source that rejects a CR missing the feature, and Dockerfile-custom-image now builds the test image with --features=rolling-updates anyway, so nothing shown makes the null case fail.

Duplicate of fp20. The null strategy deploys no UpdateSpec, which is the pre-existing default path. No operator code in the PR gates it on the feature, and the custom test image is built with --features=rolling-updates, so the claimed failure is not supported.

packages/lib/slots.ts now shifts override start/end by (invitee - organizer) offset and takes hour()*60+minute(). For example, organizer London 09:00-17:00 seen from Tokyo (+8h) gives start=1020 and end=60, and buildSlots drops it (`if (start >= end) continue`). The user's working hours were already removed for that day, and activeOverrides still filters on the unshifted date, so valid slots disappear.

The new workingHours.find(...) in checkIfIsAvailable returns true (meaning unavailable) for the first same-day interval the slot falls outside. With split hours such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 14:00 slot fails the first interval and is rejected. This is a separate bug from the golden's slotStartTime/slotEndTime mixup.

In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, `except Integration.DoesNotExist: return pipeline.next_step()` skips the new github_authenticated_user vs metadata['sender']['login'] comparison. The installation_id is user-supplied via GET/state, and build_integration only fetches /app/installations/{id}, so when the installation webhook hasn't created the row yet (delayed/failed), the security check this PR adds is bypassed.

True that BasePaginator now uses max(0, offset) for non-prev cursors while other paginators raise BadPaginationError, but clamping a tampered negative cursor to the first page is harmless (previously Django raised on negative slicing). It is only an inconsistency.

The patch target is sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, which affects only that module's single options.get call, not unrelated lookups. Each test creates new projects/org, so cache keys differ and cannot leak. Only the 'no cache/invalidate test coverage' remark is true, and that is a nit.
